sentences.text: We have gone through the contents of the application for condonation of delay along with the additional affidavit which was subsequently filed by the appellants.
After going through the same, we have no hesitation in saying that there is absolutely no explanation, much less sufficient cause shown to condone the delay.

It is true that it is not the length of the period but the explanation which is required to be considered while considering the prayer for condonation of delay, in the present case, what has been stated in the application is that after receiving certified copy of the order dated 03.05.2017, the matter was taken up for discussion and then the higher authorities of the Board decided to file an appeal.
In Para 4, it is stated that the Board issued an order on 06.01.2021 and appointed Resident Engineer as officer- incharge.
Thereafter, it has been stated that because of the COVID-19, the appeal could not be filed.
In the additional affidavit, nothing new on this aspect has been stated.
There is absolutely no explanation to condone the delay after the expiry of the period for filing the appeal till 20.03.2020.

We are referring to the aforesaid date of 20.03.2020 because on account of COVID-19 pandemic,
orders were passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the period subsequent thereafter has been excluded for the purpose of country limitation.
However, it is to be noted that in the present case the order was passed on 03.05.2017.
What the officers of the department were doing till 20.03.2020 is only a mystery.
There is absolutely no explanation for that period except a bald statement that the matter was under discussion at the level of the higher officers.

[2023/RJJD/005421] (4 of 7) [SAW-346/2022] Reliance placed by the learned counsel for the appellant on the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of G. Arumugam (supra) is wholly misconceived on facts.

That was a case where it was found that there was an attempt on the part of Rajasthan Housing Board vs Shimbhu Ram (2023/Rjjd/005421) on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13762690/

. In that case, the officer incharge was placed under suspension for corruption charges.
It is not a case of the appellants herein that it was a case of deliberate action on the part of some officers of the Board and purposely file was kept pending.

If it is not the stand of the learned counsel for the appellant, it is a case of complete negligence on the part of the officer, who in the office is dealing with the case and taking decision whether or not the appeal is to be filed.

In the two recent judgments, the Supreme Court has observed and deprecated this pratice on the part of the authorities in sitting over the matters and then filing the appeals after inordinate delay coming out with the explanation that the file remained pending in the office from one table to another.
In the case of State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors. Vs. Bherulal, 2020 SCC Online SC 849, it was found that the appeal filed by the State was with delay of 663 days.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors. Vs. Bherulal, 2020 SCC Online SC 849
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The cause shown for inordinate delay in that case was due to unavailability of documents and the process of arranging documents and also a reference to bureaucratic process works.

In the aforesaid factual context, Their Lordships of the Supreme Court, referring to its earlier decision, observed as below- [2023/RJJD/005421] (5 of 7) [SAW-346/2022] "3. No doubt, some leeway is given for the Government inefficiencies but the sad part is that the authorities keep on relying on judicial pronouncements for a period of time when technology had not advanced and a greater leeway was given to the Government (Collector, Land Acquisition, Anantnag & Anr vs. Mst. Katiji & Ors. (1987)
2 SCC 107).

entities.text:
Collector, Land Acquisition, Anantnag & Anr vs. Mst. Katiji & Ors. (1987)
2 SCC 107
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This position is more than elucidated by the judgment of this Court in Office of the Chief Post Master General & Ors. v. Living Media India Ltd. & Anr. (2012) 3 SCC 563 where the Court observed as under:
"12) It is not in dispute that the person(s) concerned were well aware or conversant with the issues involved including the prescribed period of limitation for taking up the matter by way of filing a special leave petition in this Court.

entities.text: Office of the Chief Post Master General & Ors. v. Living Media India Ltd. & Anr. (2012) 3 SCC 563
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They cannot claim that they have a separate period of limitation when the Department was possessed with competent persons familiar with court proceedings.

In the absence of plausible and acceptable explanation, we are posing a question why the delay is to be condoned mechanically merely because the Government or a wing of the Government is a party before us.

Though we are conscious of the fact that in a matter of condonation of delay when there was no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bonafide, a liberal concession has to be adopted to advance substantial justice, we are of the view that in the facts and circumstances, the Department cannot take advantage of various earlier decisions.
The claim on account of impersonal machinery and inherited bureaucratic methodology of making several notes cannot be accepted in view of the modern technologies being used and available.
The law of limitation undoubtedly binds everybody including the Government.

Rajasthan Housing Board vs Shimbhu Ram (2023/Rjjd/005421) on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13762690/
3 13) In our view, it is the right time to inform all the government bodies, their agencies and instrumentalities that unless they have reasonable and acceptable explanation for the delay and there was bonafide effort, there is no need to accept the usual explanation that the file was kept pending for several months/years due to considerable degree of procedural redtape in the process.
The government departments are under a special obligation to ensure that they perform their duties with diligence and commitment.

entities.text: Rajasthan Housing Board vs Shimbhu Ram (2023/Rjjd/005421)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Condonation of delay is an exception and should not be used as an anticipated benefit for government departments.
The law shelters everyone under the same light and should not be [2023/RJJD/005421] (6 of 7) [SAW-346/2022] swirled for the benefit of a few.

Considering the fact that there was no proper explanation offered by the Department for the delay except mentioning of various dates, according to us, the Department has miserably failed to give any acceptable and cogent reasons sufficient to condone such a huge delay."
Eight years hence the judgment is still unheeded!"

In another decision, in the case of Government of Maharashtra (Water Resources Department) V. M/s. Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Pvt. Ltd., 2021 SCC Online SC 233 also, in the factual context of long delay of 75 days, the explanation was found to be short of any sufficient cause.

entities.text: Government of Maharashtra (Water Resources Department) V. M/s. Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Pvt. Ltd., 2021 SCC Online SC 233
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The explanation in the aforesaid case was noted in para 65 of the said judgment as below - "65.
That apart, on the facts of this appeal, there is a long delay of 75 days beyond the period of 60 days provided by the Commercial Courts Act.

Despite the fact that a certified copy of the District Court's judgment was obtained by the respondent on 27.04.2019, the appeal was filed only on 09.09.2019, the explanation for delay being:
"2.
That, the certified copy of the order dated 01/04/2013 was received by the appellant on 27/04/2019.
Thereafter the matter was placed before the CGM purchase MPPKVVCL for the compliance of the order.
The same was then sent to the law officer, MPPKVVCL for opinion.
3. That after taking opinion for appeal, and approval of the concerned authorities, the officer- in-charge was appointed vide order dated 23/07/2019.

4. That, thereafter due to bulky records of the case and for procurement of the necessary documents some delay has been caused however, the appeal has been prepared and filed to pursuant to the same and further delay.

5. That due to the aforesaid procedural approval and since the appellant is a public entity formed under the Energy department of the State Government, the delay caused in filing the appeal is bonafide and which deserve[s] to be condoned."

entities.text: Rajasthan Housing Board vs Shimbhu Ram (2023/Rjjd/005421)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This explanation falls woefully short of making out any sufficient cause.
This appeal is therefore allowed and the condonation of delay is set aside on this score also."

Taking into consideration the cause shown in the application for condonation of delay and in the light of observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the aforesaid two cases, we find ourselves unable to condone the delay in absence of sufficient cause.

Accordingly, the application No.01/2022 for condonation of delay is dismissed and consequently,
the appeal is also dismissed.
